author.name: Requirements Reuben
author.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.

challenge.name: The Committed Pallets
challenge.description: A supplier has confirmed a bulk order for a middle aisle promotion that ships next week, leaving no room for model error. #requirements_reuben# insists the acceptance criteria must be fully governed to guarantee the allocation logic is auditable before the trucks leave. #reliability_ruth# argues the criteria are sufficient as manual checks because the physical stock is already committed and the team needs to ship the feature immediately to handle the live orders.

output.content: I need the hand over between risk and acceptance, and the hand over from acceptance to evaluation, to run without a person in the loop. When these steps are done by hand, the data integrity is compromised, and the audit trail becomes a mess of manual entries. I want the pipeline to trigger the next stage automatically once the previous one clears. The more automated this chain is, the stronger our guarantee that the allocation logic is sound before the trucks leave. I am not asking for a new tool, just for the existing checks to fire the next job on their own. This reduces the chance of a silent failure and ensures the system is fully governed from start to finish.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states that increasing the level of automation in the chain makes them happier by strengthening guarantees and reducing silent failures, indicating that doing more than the minimum asked aligns with their core need.
